items.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Kenny Burrell was responsible for us meeting, in the sense that he had me come play a duet for the Grammy pre-

ctx.x: Yeah, it’s wonderful. It’s just a wonderful ensemble. I like the exposure and the color that we get together. I played – I sat in with them when they played the other night in the Philippines, because they were there too. We played two nights. They played two

nights, but not the same nights. So she invited me to play with them the night before we left. I sat in, played a couple of tunes with them, which she loves, because she likes that combination, flute and vocal. Kenny Burrell was responsible for us meeting, in the sense that he had me come play a duet for the Grammy pre- – Grammy museum, pre-Grammy awards, two years ago. That’s when she was there with Alan Bergman. You know the guy?

items.title: Kenny Burrell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: …And, plus the fact it was a big- celebrate my 75th so that was going to draw some crowds anyway. It was a tremendous week. I mean they had lines around the block, you know. And so I can’t say enough about it. Gerald is always easy to work with so we talked about the music—it was not any, not any problem—and figured out what to do and so I had stuff with the big band. And what else did…? I had Joey DeFrancesco, right? On with a trio with the organ; and I had Hubert Laws…
